title: Frontline Coaching and Session Documentation Agent

approval.note: A composed script is a draft. A human reads it before this film is published anywhere.

script.vo01: Managers spend a large part of the week writing up conversations they have already had. Coaching forms have their own structure, and completing one properly is a task in its own right after the session ends.
script.vo02: Customer conversations are summarised from memory and pushed into the CRM by hand, so the record is only as good as the day allowed.
script.vo03: It reads Session recordings and transcripts, Coaching form templates. It engages you in Microsoft Teams and Dynamics 365. And it can capture the session and draft the write-up as it happens, showing the reasoning behind every answer.
script.vo04: A manager finishes a coaching session and asks for the write-up. The agent completes the standard form from the conversation itself, quoting the moments each observation rests on.
script.vo05: Asked for the next steps, the agent lists what was agreed and who owns each item, then offers to write them straight into the customer record.
script.vo06: On risk, the agent separates what the manager actually said from what it inferred, and holds back anything sensitive that does not belong in a shared record.
script.vo_payoff: Managers leave the session with the record already written and the next steps already captured.
script.vo_helps: The result? Documentation time returned to coaching, the write-up produced as a by-product, and a record that stays current.
script.vo_cta: Get started on your agentic journey today. Talk to your Microsoft representative to learn more.
